text:
Brandt Clarke has quietly become the Kings' best defenseman by the chances. Los Angeles has 59% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, almost 14 points better than without him, and he has 14 points in 19 games after 40 in 82 last season.

Our numbers think that undersells him. The Kings have scored 7.6 fewer goals than their chances with Clarke out there, which has cost him points, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back. It fits a pattern: Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season (his team created more with him on, 91st percentile among defensemen), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 99th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists and stopping more entries at his own line than most.

One caution goes the other way. His own goals (three on 1.5 expected) are running hot, and our range has his scoring rate drifting down from 2.3 points per 60 toward 1.6. But on a Kings team whose record is worse than its play, Clarke is one of the reasons the play is good.
